analysis:
Both units are base-side excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 5236-5682). The PR change is documentation only. The visible patch excerpt covers served-record scoping (serving scope, tensorAssistant), a tp-check --layer-stride flag and other ranges. The excerpt is truncated, and the head text for most changed ranges is not supplied. I found no executable code, no new endpoints, and no changes to crypto, authorization, attestation or key handling.

The base text covers MiMo and GLM tensor-parallel speculative rounds, placement, GLM media, and the prefix-cache tenant partitions (prefixScope, prefixDiskScope), which relate to T-041. It also covers sealed AES-GCM all-sums, the load agreement binding the decode policy, and the worker environment switches. These are not changed in the visible patch. The new patch text about recording the serving scope (darkbloom or local) and the tensorAssistant flag affects only planner and calibration record selection. It is a performance-routing concern, not a confidentiality or authorization boundary. The visible text does not weaken the T-041 account-scoped cache isolation or the TTL/KEK posture.

Unverified: the actual source changes behind these docs, in particular --layer-stride (a diagnostic flag), ClusterServedSpeedRecords filtering and the later changed hunks (lines ~4866-4891, 6725-6735, 6858-6894, 7318-7454 on head). These are not visible in the supplied units. I cannot rule out documentation drift or code changes elsewhere. The remaining units and the code need review if any later hunk touches security claims such as tenant partitions or the prefix SSD tier. No finding qualifies from the supplied evidence.
